full_judgment:
Latifur Rahman, J:- This appeal by leave by defendant No. 2- Government is against the judgment and order dated 27.4.94 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division allowing Appeal from Original Decree No.23 of 1990 thereby setting aside the judgment and decree dated 23.9.87 passed by the Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 118 of 1985, in a suit for specific performance of contract. 

 2. Respondent No. 1 as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 632 of 1982 in the 2nd Court of Subordinate judge, Dhaka impleading the appellant as defendant No.2 praying for a decree for specific performance of contract against defendant No. 1, who is respondent No. 2 in. this appeal alleging that Syed Abdul Hadi was the original owner of the suit property at G/31, Zakir Hossain Road, Mohammadpur Housing Estate, Dhaka from whom defendant No. 1. Mahmood Alam purchased the property by a registered deed of sale dated 14-12-62.  The plaintiff-respondent contracted to purchase the property by a deed of agreement for sale from Mahmood Alam 27-1 -71 for a consideration Of 'II. 80,000/- out of which Tk. 20,000/- was paid on the date of agreement as earnest money. Subsequently on 12-12-72, 9-11-74 and 9-12-79 Mahmood Alam took Tk. 20,000/- Tk. 10,000/- and Tk. 10,000/- respectively endorsing receipts thereof on the back page of the agreement. The suit property was listed as an abandoned property and one  Abdul Wahed (defendant No. 4) took allotment thereof Subsequently the Government released the property and directed Abdul Wahed to vacate the same. The plaintiff was confirmed on 1-10-82 that Mahmood Alam would not voluntarily execute and register a sale deed in her favour on receipt of the balance consideration money of Tk. 20,000/-. Hence the suit. 

 5. On appeal, F.A. No. 23 of 1990, a Division Bench of the High Court Division by judgment and order  dated 27-4-94 allowed the same and set aside the judgment and decree of the trial court. 

 7. The learned Judges of the High Court Division on consideration of the materials on record and the application for additional evidence found that the Government released the suit property from the list of abandoned property under Article 15 of P.O.  No. 16 of 1972 and also found that the, deed of agreement stands proved by P. W. 2 who was an attesting witness to the said deed and who apart from proving his signature therein also stated that the executants (Mahmood Alam) put his signature in his presence and that he knew his signature. The High Court Division found that the original title deed of Syed Abdul Hadi, Ext. 1 and the original allotment letter dated 1-1-60 in favour of Syed Abdul Hadi were corning from the custody of the plaintiff and taking these relevant facts into consideration it allowed the appeal and decreed the suit with a direction to defendant No.4 to vacate the suit property. 

 allottee of the Government who cross-examined this witness before the High Court Division. The learned Judges of the High Court Division should not have accepted this deed of agreement dated 27.1.71 which was produced before the High Court Division for the first time without examining the executants Mahmood Alam or without inquiring as to his whereabouts. As a matter of fact this filing of this deed of agreement at a belated stage without sufficiently explaining the cause for not filing this document in the suit, more particularly when the respondent stated in Ext. 2 that she would not produce any more witness and would not produce any document in her favour before the Trial Court. From the materials on record it is also found from the Gazette Notification of September 20, 1988 that the property is listed as an abandoned building under Supplementary Provision Ordinance, LIV of 1985. The trial court found that the plaintiff could not say as to the whereabouts of her vendor and in that view doubted the deed of agreement and dismissed the suit for specific performance of contract. The learned Judges totally failed to consider the fact that the bainapatra was of a doubtful nature which was the positive finding of the trial court. In a suit for specific performance of contract the genuineness of the agreement of sale was the prime consideration to which the judicial mind of the Judges were not attracted and thereby they wrongly decreed the suit.
